author: pandoleena

title: Great tool!
body: I started with the trial and do not regret getting the full access. The mixture of learning, practice and chatting is great. I feel like I am learning something new daily that actually helps me with my everyday life, and it fits into my tight work schedule. It also helps alot if you have undiagnosed ADHD. Very well developed app! Can totally recommend!
author: Marie_Louise_23

title: Information on adhd in women very Basic
body:
I’m really disappointed in the material on women with ADHD. It is labelled as „unique experience“ and hidden in the app, even though you are asked in the survey about your gender and how you indentify. The focus in that category is almost entirely on partnerships and children, as if women were only meant to have babies and boyfriends and that’s all we could possibly want. Only a few sentences acknowledge the broader reality of women who live independently or choose different paths.

Just because many of your clients may be in their 40s with children does not mean this represents all women struggling with adhd. The material could have been structured to reflect different life situations. What about women in their teens, 20s, or those in their 30s, who don’t want children or a partner - regardless of being heterosexual? Not to mention the queer community. Much of what you present here can already be found in countless ADHD podcasts. In fact, some podcasts hosted by men cover women’s ADHD experiences more thoughtfully than this app does.

It’s 2025, and yet you’re still reproducing outdated gender roles while presenting yourself as knowledgeable about ADHD in women. And when it comes to men, the conversation doesn’t immediately revolve around household chores or children or EVEN partnerships. What a coincidence.

The material on hormones and ADHD is also extremely limited. The explanation is not really detailed and very basic. Not really more on the science on PMDD and hormonal cycles in general. If you really want to understand how to manage your hormonal cycle you need to search elsewhere for further information. There are no meaningful, practical tips on how to manage ADHD symptoms throughout the cycle besides some essential oils (don’t get me wrong oils can help).

body: Wirkt wie eine richtig gute App, aber sie hätten ruhig sagen können dass es 50€/Monat kostet, bevor man die ganze Anmeldung durchläuft....
author: Lensi123

title: Super bis auf wenige Ausnahmen
body:
Ich liebe diese App. 2 Dinge stören mich aber erheblich. Die Live Events sind von den Zeiten her eher weniger für den europäischen Raum geeignet…. Daher fände ich es angemessen, die
Preise zu senken, bis dies geändert ist. Außerdem ist plötzlich die to do List Funktion verschwunden, welche ich sehr nützlich fand. Auch die Nachrichtenfunktion ist verschwunden. Vorher war es möglich mit einem „Trainer“ zu sprechen…Ärgerlich. Bis dahin leider nur 3 Sterne, sonst wären es 5.
author: jenepre

title: loving the app so far
body: Just started my journey, I have tried so many health apps like Ahead and Headspace and while I do like them too, this app really is at the core of my Adhd problems, it feels like it is made for me. I feel understood and though it‘s quite pricy in comparison to the above mentioned, I think it‘s worth a try and see how often you use it because having Adhd makes it so hard to stick to a new routine, especially if it‘s not giving dopamine out like from a candy box.

body:

So sad :(
author: keniajahnk

title: Mind blowing
body: This is the first time I write a review. But I am so thankful for this app. I am not diagnosed with ADHS, but it helps me in my everyday life so much. I am so glad I invested the money.
author: Kidswatch121

title: Too expensive
body:
I subscribed to it because I wanted to try out the free trial. I then got a mail that the free trial was over and I had to pay for my subscription (229€ annually I believe) which is impossible for me to do as a student. This particular e-Mail also said that I was being charged if I didn’t cancel the subscription within 24 hours. Obviously I didn’t cancel (people with ADHD can be very forgetful) because I read the mail too late. 
Let’s see where this goes:) 
In general, I’d also say that the app is absolutely overpriced and for the most part useless, since you might as well go to therapy and have actual face to face conversations for the high prices they charge.
author: unbekannter homo sapiens

title: Charged before free trial
body: The app was marketed to me, that I will get a free trial before paying. I was charged immediately. As I am before receiving my salary, it’s a problem. Now I have to wait for 2 days to get an e-mail answer about it and I had an exact amount of money on my account to send my bills… the app was supposed to help with organization and stress and it only brought more stress as of now. That leaves a very bad taste and I don’t know if I want to use it anymore, can’t trust the informations about pricing that I’m being given.
author: Aleksandra Pieklo

title: Would help me probably but
body:
As a jobless person struggling financially these price politics are a slap in my face. No money, no help in finding better tools and strategies.
Sorry, but many adhd people have financial problems and this is not respected here. The prices are much to high. It’s an app, not a therapist.
author: miss_off

title: Very confusing pricing
body:
When I check in the subscription section of my Apple ID it lists multiple entries with different prices for the same thing.
Monthly/annual without coaching is listed twice with different prices for the exact same thing and once with coaching. Also 6 month with coaching is available for 230€ while annual with coaching is only 215€. (Why would anyone take 6 month?)
For an app that tries to help people with ADHD this is very confusing.
The app seems great but I would love a clear communication about prices before I subscribe. Maybe ask one of the mental health professionals you employ for help with the design of the pricing tables.

title: Only yearly subscription?
body: I made use of the offer to test the app for 5 (or 7?) days and have really benefitted from it, so I would actually give a four or even five star rating- but I feel the annual subscription of more than 200 Euro is too much. With a monthly or 3months subscription I would have kept the app, but now like that!
author: MartinK.

title: I wish…
body:
There was greater variation in types of subscription / discounts or accommodations for low income people, students, etc. 

You could give limited access, for example, only to courses and exercises and without personal coaching, as I do get that this is kind of tailored service is high-value. 

As a graduate student struggling to manage myself every single day, I could especially use the help — but of course it is precisely being a student that imposes certain limitations on income and available resources.
